index.title: Project overview
index.heading: Product entity matching with RoBERTa and comparison features
index.lead: Compare retailer listings using their text and product fields. The model combines a joint text representation with explicit comparisons of titles, model numbers, brands and prices, and returns a score for each pair.
index.description: Product matching examples, RoBERTa and comparison features, fixed-pool results and code entry points.

method.heading: Data preparation and RoBERTa feature fusion
method.lead: Follow the product pairs from their project data roles through field normalization, explicit comparisons and joint RoBERTa encoding. The model scores both listing orders and combines three training seeds; development and calibration data choose the checkpoint and cutoff.
method.description: Data source and roles, normalization, 42 comparison features, RoBERTa fusion, aggregation and calibration.

results.title: Results
results.heading: Retrospective results on [[evaluation]] product pairs

overview_close_title: Use the code and explore the project
overview_close_p: The repository includes model source, fixed settings, six-method results and bilingual guides. The quickstart checks the public code and opens this static site locally. To run model prediction, supply the product inputs, model snapshots and trained weights described in the reproduction guide.
roles_intro: The four roles below are project assignments. Fit estimates model parameters and title IDF (inverse document frequency), which downweights words that occur in many training titles. Development selects one shared checkpoint epoch, calibration selects a decision cutoff, and evaluation supplies the reported comparison.
role_p: Fit title IDF, the numerical-feature references and the models for each training seed.
Use the three seeds’ predictions to select one common epoch.
Select a cutoff by calibration F1, then precision, then the higher cutoff.
Apply the saved cutoff and report ranking metrics and prediction counts.
roles_note: Only fit inputs include target labels. Other roles store labels separately and join them to scores by pair_id in selection or metric commands; preparation reuses the saved fit IDF state. These input rules do not establish an untouched official test split or an entity-disjoint evaluation. The fixed pool’s historical exposure record is incomplete.
processing_names: Title IDF fitted on fit records
processing_p: Text comparison uses Unicode normalization, case folding and whitespace cleanup. Missing brand, description, model and category values remain missing; the feature vector records presence indicators where defined. Two absent values are not counted as a positive equality comparison.

A plain nonnegative decimal can be parsed as a price. Ambiguous symbols or separators keep an unresolved quality state. Price similarity is enabled only when both prices parse and their recognized currency codes agree; otherwise the comparable-price indicator is zero. No exchange-rate conversion or price imputation is applied.

Model-like title codes are extracted and compared as sets. Features describe exact overlap, normalized edit similarity and shared letters with different digits or shared digits with different letters. Native model numbers are compared separately and checked against the opposite listing’s title codes.

Title word and character document frequencies are fitted on content-deduplicated business records from fit only. The saved IDF state weights title overlap in later roles without refitting. Direct title-number and compact-title comparisons are also included; they do not require fitting. For example, in 100 synthetic training records, a term appearing in 80 of those records has weight 1 + ln(101/81) ≈ 1.221; one appearing in two records has weight 1 + ln(101/3) ≈ 4.517. Common terms therefore contribute less evidence of overlap. These counts illustrate the calculation; they are not dataset statistics.
features_intro: Each pair receives a [[features]]-dimensional comparison vector, named x42 in the code. Its four groups contain 14, 8, 8 and 12 values in the FEATURES.json order. IDs and labels are excluded. Similarities for missing inputs are zero, with separate presence or comparability indicators where defined. Expand a group to inspect the identifiers and meanings.
feature_group_names: Title IDF and direct title comparisons
feature_group_p: Fourteen values compare title and description tokens, brand agreement, numeric tokens, title length and prices. Presence and price-comparability indicators distinguish unavailable evidence from a measured similarity.

Eight values contain four IDF-weighted title similarities and four direct comparisons of mixed alphanumeric tokens, numeric tokens, numeric presence and compact-title equality. Only the IDF state is fitted, using fit records.
Eight values compare model-like codes extracted from titles. They cover missingness, exact overlap, set overlap, best edit similarity and differences in the letter and digit parts.
Twelve values compare native model numbers and categories, including presence, equality, edit/trigram similarity and whether a native model appears in the other listing’s title codes.
architecture_title: RoBERTa text encoding and feature-fusion head
architecture_intro: The model combines a joint text representation with the x42 comparison vector. AB means listing A followed by B; BA reverses that order. Each training seed has its own fitted parameters and scores both orders with the same architecture.
configuration_intro: Training follows a six-epoch schedule. Development compares ensemble predictions and selects common epoch [[epoch]] for seeds [[seeds]]. Calibration selects cutoff [[threshold]], which is then reused for evaluation.
precision_training: BF16 (16-bit brain floating point) encoder computations; FP32 (32-bit floating point) parameters and head
comparison_title: AP ranking and F1 at calibrated cutoffs
comparison_intro: All six methods score the same [[evaluation]]-pair retrospective pool, including [[positive]] matches. Average precision (AP) measures ranking from continuous scores; F1 combines precision and recall at each method’s own calibration cutoff. Both plot axes cover 0–1.
chart_f1_title: F1 at each method’s calibration cutoff
nojs: Both complete plots remain visible when JavaScript is disabled.

methods.S33: L30 plus three MiniLM semantic/missingness features
methods.C0: Independently trained RoBERTa control with x42 zeroed

table_caption: Metrics are shown to six decimal places, except P@100, which uses two. The downloadable CSV preserves the original unrounded values, integer counts and each calibration cutoff.
matrix_title: C+ confusion matrix at the calibration cutoff
matrix_caption: Rows are actual classes; columns are predictions. [[evaluation]] pairs in total, with [[positive]] actual matches.
matrix_note: At cutoff [[threshold]], C+ predicts [[fp]] nonmatches as matches and misses [[fn]] actual matches. These counts give precision [[precision4]] and recall [[recall4]]. They describe matching predictions on this pool, not actual catalog merges.
delta_title: C+ differences from L42 and C0
definition_p: Average precision (AP) summarizes precision over the ranking of positive pairs. It uses the continuous pair scores and groups tied scores. AP [[ap4]] is not a classification accuracy of [[ap4]].

F1 combines precision and recall after turning scores into match/nonmatch predictions at a cutoff. The cutoff is selected on calibration labels and fixed before evaluation. Changing it changes the balance of false matches and missed matches.

P@100 is the fraction of actual matches among the first 100 ranked pairs. Score ties at the boundary are ordered by pair_id. P@100 [[p100]] describes those 100 pairs in this pool, rather than all products or future listings.
public_title: Check the public code and saved outputs
public_intro: After setting up the environment above, run these checks from the repository root. They exercise input interfaces, feature calculations and metric arithmetic using synthetic records, and check the stored aggregate results. They require no model download or GPU.
check_step_title: Interfaces, saved outputs and file checks
check_step_p: public_smoke.py checks the package and CLI entry points. run_notebook.py runs the English and Chinese executable walkthroughs and compares their saved outputs. verify_public_release.py checks the public file inventory, hashes, local links and result arithmetic. A passed report confirms these code and document checks; it does not run model inference.
tests_step_title: Command-line help and synthetic input tests
tests_step_p: The command-line interface (CLI) exposes preparation, training and prediction commands. The test suite checks synthetic cases; passing it does not reproduce the trained model’s experimental results.
replay_intro: The public code entry ran [[replay_commands]] commands with original frozen inputs and local model artifacts. [[replay_groups]] independently checked result groups matched the saved outputs; the maximum prediction difference was [[max_difference]]. The replay covered input preparation and existing-model predictions. It did not fit new weights or evaluate an independent new Walmart–Amazon sample.

Existing-weight replay requires local snapshots and trusted weights; fresh end-to-end training and independent new Walmart–Amazon sample evaluation remain unvalidated.

rebuild_check_p: The check command generates in memory and compares every generated byte. It does not write files.

data_example_intro: The three synthetic Acme drill scenarios show normalized fields and eight of the 42 comparisons. The first changes model spelling and brand capitalization, the second changes a model digit, and the third removes a brand and changes currency. Here a token means a text fragment produced by the feature tokenizer.
model_decision_explanation: RoBERTa reads the two listings together to represent their text. A separate 42-value vector records explicit comparisons, such as model-digit differences, missing brands and whether prices share a currency. Brand, model number, category and title enter the text branch; description and price contribute through the comparison features. The two branches are combined to produce a pair score.
result_interpretation: Compared with L42, the strongest numerical-feature reference on this pool, C+ reduces false matches from [[reference_fp]] to [[fp]] while missed matches increase from [[reference_fn]] to [[fn]], improving F1. AP is only [[delta_c0_ap]] percentage points above independently trained C0, so this comparison does not establish a substantial ranking gain from the 42 features.
model_definition: C+ names the final model in this project: RoBERTa with 42 comparison features, averaged across three training seeds.
quickstart_intro: Install Git and Python 3.11 or newer, then clone the repository. These checks and the local website use only the Python standard library. The project environment below keeps any later dependencies separate from your other projects.
quickstart_preview: The smoke check prints a JSON report with status passed. Keep the server running and open the local project site below; Ctrl+C stops the server.
quickstart_python: Commands below explicitly use the project interpreter: .venv/bin/python on macOS/Linux and .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe on Windows. Choose the block for your system. If you downloaded a ZIP, enter its extracted repository folder and start with the environment commands.
quickstart_gpu: Real input preparation and model prediction require locally supplied product data, model snapshots and checkpoints. Follow the linked guide for the GPU environment and working directories; the documented CUDA setup was checked on Windows 11 with an RTX 3060.
quickstart_gpu_link: GPU environment and required local files
data_context: The experiment uses a custom fixed set of product pairs from Walmart and Amazon. A pair contains two retailer records, and its label indicates whether they refer to the same product. The reported evaluation pool contains [[evaluation]] pairs: [[positive]] matches and [[negative]] nonmatches.
data_card_link: Data fields, role reconstruction and access requirements
processing_intro: Preparation keeps normalized business fields and native model/category fields in separate views. It produces comparable values without replacing missing or ambiguous source values. The rules below are shared by the numerical-feature models and the neural model. A token is a text fragment produced by a tokenizer; the feature calculations below use their own tokenization rules.
normalization_example_note: These teaching values are computed by the public normalization functions when the site is built. Ordinary text retains hyphens; separate compact model/title views remove separators. Currency symbols and commas remain ambiguous, and missing prices remain missing.
architecture_output: One raw score (logit) per direction enters the aggregation below.
architecture_budget_title: Text length and field token budgets
architecture_budget_p: A token is a text unit produced by the model’s tokenizer. Each record has budgets of 16 tokens for brand, 32 for native model number, 16 for category and 62 for title. A long title retains its first 40 and last 22 tokens. The two records use at most 252 tokens; four special tokens bring the pair limit to 256.
aggregation_p: A logit is the classifier’s raw score before conversion to a probability. Within each seed, average the AB and BA logits, then apply sigmoid to map the result into 0–1. Take the equal mean of those probabilities across seeds [[seeds]]. This gives a score symmetric to exchanging the two listings, while preserving the distinction between averaging logits and averaging probabilities.
aggregation_note: All three seeds use the common epoch [[epoch]] selected on development data. The final score is classified as a match when it is at or above the calibration cutoff [[threshold]].
calibration_p: Calibration maximizes F1, breaking ties by precision and then the higher cutoff. Evaluation labels are kept separate from model inputs and are not used to choose these settings. The table below records the settings of the reported experiment.
read_scope: Read the evaluation scope and limitations
reference_control_note: C0 is trained independently of C+, with all 42 comparison values zero throughout training and inference. It retains the neural dimensions and uses the six-epoch scheduler for four training epochs; the comparison uses epoch 4.
chart_ap_caption: C+ and the independently trained C0 have nearly equal AP; their difference is only [[delta_c0_ap]] percentage points.
chart_f1_caption: Each F1 value uses that method’s calibration cutoff; the bars show no confidence intervals.
gains_intro: The chart shows absolute metric differences on the same pool, using a shared 0–6 percentage-point scale (pp).
gains_caption: No confidence intervals are available, so the bar lengths do not establish statistical significance or a substantial feature-driven ranking gain.
outcomes_title: Correct and incorrect outcomes within each actual class
outcomes_intro: Each bar is normalized to 100%; the denominators differ: [[positive]] matches and [[negative]] nonmatches.
outcomes_tradeoff: Compared with L42, false matches fall from [[reference_fp]] to [[fp]] and missed matches rise from [[reference_fn]] to [[fn]]. Higher F1 comes with a small recall decrease. Aggregate counts do not identify which particular pairs were corrected.
example_boundary: These synthetic listings illustrate field and feature calculations. The public functions compute comparison values when the pages are built, and the buttons switch between the generated scenario tables. This example runs no RoBERTa inference.
command_flow_intro: These command-line interface (CLI) stages connect pair preparation, model training, prediction and evaluation. Model runs require local product inputs, pinned dependencies and model files. The guide gives file formats and full arguments for each stage.
checkpoint_note: Hashes identify the local weights corresponding to these checkpoints. The public repository does not redistribute model weights.

overview_brief.title: The matching task
overview_brief.text: The same product can have different titles, model-number spellings or missing fields at different retailers. Finding the corresponding records helps align catalogs and inspect duplicates.

overview_brief.title: Input and output
overview_brief.text: Input is a pair of product records with title, brand, description, price, currency, native model number and category. The model returns a score from 0 to 1; a calibrated cutoff turns it into a match or nonmatch prediction.

spelling.title: Model spelling
spelling.note: Title token overlap is 0.5 because ZX-100 and ZX100 form different tokens. Compact-model equality and title-code overlap are both 1, preserving their agreement despite spelling.

digits.title: Different model digits
digits.note: Title token overlap remains 0.5, but compact-model equality is 0 and the digit-conflict feature is 1. These values are evidence supplied to the model; the example does not predict a match or rejection.

missing.title: Missing brand / different currency
missing.note: A missing brand does not count as an equal brand. Both prices parse, but USD and EUR differ, so price comparability and similarity are 0. The comparability indicator distinguishes this unavailable comparison from a measured similarity.

architecture_nodes.title: Field serialization
architecture_nodes.text: Serialize brand, native model number, category and title from both listings in each order. Description and price are handled by the comparison branch.

architecture_nodes.title: Joint pair encoding
architecture_nodes.text: RoBERTa jointly reads the complete pair. CLS denotes its first-token representation, used to summarize the pair. A linear projection and GELU (Gaussian Error Linear Unit), a nonlinear activation, transform this 768-dimensional state into 64 values.

architecture_nodes.title: Explicit comparisons
architecture_nodes.text: Compare business fields, title evidence, title codes and native model/category fields. Presence and price comparability have separate indicators. Title IDF uses fit records only.

architecture_nodes.title: Shared comparison vector
architecture_nodes.text: The same vector is supplied for AB and BA. It includes description, price and currency evidence that is absent from the text serialization.

architecture_nodes.title: Concatenation and classifier
architecture_nodes.text: Concatenate the text projection and comparisons, then apply a 64-unit GELU layer, dropout [[dropout]] and a linear output. Training updates both the encoder and classifier.

model_resource_blocks.title: Input
model_resource_blocks.text: Two retailer records. Title, brand, native model number and category form the text input; description, price, currency and missing-field states contribute through comparison features.

model_resource_blocks.title: Architecture
model_resource_blocks.text: RoBERTa jointly encodes the pair, projects its 768-dimensional representation to 64 values and joins [[features]] comparisons. The 106 → 64 → 1 classifier returns a raw score, called a logit.

model_resource_blocks.title: Scoring and decision
model_resource_blocks.text: AB and BA are the two listing orders. Within each seed, average their logits and apply sigmoid. Average the resulting probabilities across seeds [[seeds]]. A final score at or above [[threshold]] is classified as a match.

reference_methods.B22: Logistic regression on the first 22 comparison features.
reference_methods.S33: L30 plus three fixed MiniLM text-similarity and missingness features.
reference_methods.L42: Gradient-boosted trees on all 42 comparisons; the strongest numerical-feature reference on this pool.
reference_methods.C+: RoBERTa pair encoding with 42 comparisons, averaged across three training seeds.
reference_methods.C0: A RoBERTa control with the comparison-feature input set to zero.

limits_paragraphs: The [[evaluation]]-pair evaluation pool is retrospective and its historical use is not fully documented. The current label-separation interface does not resolve that history. An independent new Walmart–Amazon sample or an entity-disjoint evaluation has not been established.

C+ improves AP and F1 over L42 on this pool, but its AP is only [[delta_c0_ap]] percentage points above independently trained C0. The aggregate results do not establish a substantial feature-driven ranking gain or statistical significance; no confidence intervals are available.

Existing-weight replay verifies artifact preparation and prediction through the public code entry. It does not reproduce fresh end-to-end training or supply new unseen-data evidence. Production latency and business benefits have not been measured, and pair scores alone do not justify automatic catalog merging.
